backlog.spec: Before the repair step, sort the circles by their radii in descending order. When calculating the shrinking factors, prioritize preserving larger circles.
backlog.title: Pre-sort radii by magnitude

backlog.spec: Instead of full random restarts, use a shrinking window for the time budget where the number of SLSQP iterations decreases as time runs out.
backlog.title: Multistart SLSQP with adaptive size

backlog.spec: Initialize centers using a Sobol sequence or a blue noise distribution instead of uniform random noise to achieve better coverage.
backlog.title: Guided initialization for centers

backlog.spec: During the SLSQP phase, start with a very small radius for all circles and gradually increase the target sum of radii to avoid early local optima.
backlog.title: Gradual radius scaling

backlog.spec: In the SLSQP objective function, add a penalty term for circles exceeding the [0,1] boundary to keep the optimizer in the feasible region longer.
backlog.title: Soft penalty interior constraints

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, run a brief Simulated Annealing phase where circles are slightly jittered and radii are adjusted based on a temperature schedule.
backlog.title: Simulated Annealing local search

backlog.spec: After the repair step, take the repaired (c, r) as the new x0 and run a few iterations of SLSQP to 'relax' the shrinkage.
backlog.title: Iterative repair and re-optimize

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to a value relative to $1/	ext{sqrt}(n)$ (e.g., $0.1 / 	ext{sqrt}(n)$) rather than a constant 0.05.
backlog.title: Dynamic INIT_RADIUS

backlog.spec: Optimize x-coordinates and y-coordinates separately in alternating steps to simplify the gradient landscape.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise optimization

backlog.spec: Remove constraints and replace them with a high-penalty term in the objective function: $\sum r_i - \lambda \sum 	ext{overlap}(i, j)$.
backlog.title: Penalty method for overlaps

backlog.spec: Replace uniform initialization with a greedy placement where circles are placed one-by-one in the best available spot.
backlog.title: Greedy initial placement

backlog.spec: Use SLSQP for the initial rough packing and switch to L-BFGS-B for fine-tuning once the constraints are mostly satisfied.
backlog.title: L-BFGS-B transition

backlog.spec: In the repair step, when shrinking $r[i]$ and $r[j]$, shrink them proportionally to their current radii to preserve the larger circle's volume.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted repair

backlog.spec: Divide the 30s time limit into 4 chunks; run 4 independent `solve_once` tasks and keep the best result (simulated by sequential loops).
backlog.title: Parallel independent restarts

backlog.spec: Initialize circles more densely near the edges and corners, where packing density often peaks in optimal solutions.
backlog.title: Boundary-aware initialization

backlog.spec: Optimize the packing of $k$ circles ($k < 32$) first, then add the $(k+1)$-th circle and re-optimize all.
backlog.title: Sequential Circle Addition

backlog.spec: Treat circles as particles connected by springs that repel each other; use a velocity-based update for 50 iterations to resolve overlaps.
backlog.title: Elastic Band repair

backlog.spec: Replace SLSQP with a custom gradient descent step using momentum for the radii and centers to escape local minima.
backlog.title: Gradient Descent with Momentum

backlog.spec: During the repair step, allow the centers $(c_x, c_y)$ to move slightly to resolve overlaps instead of only shrinking the radii.
backlog.title: Shrinkage with rotation

backlog.spec: Stop SLSQP early if the objective hasn't improved significantly in 10 iterations to allow for more random restarts.
backlog.title: Early exit SLSQP

backlog.spec: Apply a non-linear scaling to the objective function: maximize $\sum r_i^k$ for $k > 1$ to favor larger circles, then map back to $\sum r_i$.
backlog.title: Non-linear Scaling

backlog.spec: During the repair loop, add a tiny amount of random noise to the centers to help 'shake' the circles out of local configurations.
backlog.title: Jittered Repair

backlog.spec: Initialize $x0$ based on a known configuration of 31 circles and then optimize the 32nd circle into the remaining space.
backlog.title: Hard-coded Circle Template

backlog.spec: Run a loop: Solve $\rightarrow$ Repair $\rightarrow$ Slightly grow radii $\rightarrow$ Solve again. Repeat until the time limit.
backlog.title: Iterative Shrink-and-Grow

backlog.spec: In the repair loop, use a step size that decreases over time (cooling) to stabilize the packing.
backlog.title: Variable Step Repair

backlog.spec: Identify only the circles that are overlapping or out of bounds and only include them in the repair calculation.
backlog.title: Active Set Repair

backlog.spec: Normalize the gradient of the sum of radii by the sum of radii to ensure consistent step sizes during optimization.
backlog.title: Normalized Gradient

backlog.spec: Optimize a weighted sum of $\sum r_i$ and a 'spread' metric (variance of $r_i$) to encourage a diverse range of sizes.
backlog.title: Multi-objective optimization

backlog.spec: Instead of keeping the absolute best, keep a weighted average of the best results to favor 'stable' configurations.
backlog.title: Time-weighted best

backlog.spec: Randomly vary the `maxiter` and `ftol` parameters in each `solve_once` call to explore different optimization behaviors.
backlog.title: Randomized SLSQP options

backlog.spec: Instead of using SLSQP for every restart, use a simple Gradient Descent with Momentum for a set number of iterations to explore the landscape, then switch to SLSQP for a final polish. This might help escape local minima more effectively than the standard SLSQP starting point.
backlog.title: Momentum-based Gradient Descent Restart

backlog.spec: After finding a good packing with the current staged SLSQP approach, take the best result and apply a small random perturbation (jitter) to the centers and radii, then run a very short SLSQP refinement (e.g., 20-50 iterations). Repeat this until the time limit is reached.
backlog.title: Iterative Basin Hopping

backlog.spec: Modify the _repair function so that when two circles overlap, the radius reduction is weighted by the circle's current radius. Circles with larger radii should 'give' less than smaller circles, potentially preserving the larger circles that contribute more to the sum.
backlog.title: Radius-Weighted Repair

backlog.spec: Replace the hard inequality constraints (c, 0) >= r, etc., with a penalty term in the objective function: -sum(r) + lambda * sum(max(0, r - (c_0 - epsilon))^2). Use a high lambda. This can sometimes lead to smoother gradients and better convergence in SLSQP.
backlog.title: Soft Penalty Interior Constraints

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed INIT_RADIUS, sample the initial radii from a distribution where the mean is proportional to the area of the unit square divided by n, adjusted by a 'packing density' factor (e.g., 0.7). This ensures the starting point is more 'dense' on average.
backlog.title: Dynamic INIT_RADIUS

backlog.spec: Instead of capping all radii at 0.1, 0.2, etc., grow only the smallest radii first in the stages. This prevents any single circle from dominating the optimization path too early and may allow for more diverse packing structures.
backlog.title: Sequential Radius Growth

backlog.spec: Initialize the circles such that they are more likely to be placed near the boundaries or in corners. Use a distribution that favors the edges of the unit square, as high-quality packings often have many circles tangent to the boundary.
backlog.title: Boundary-Aware Initialization

backlog.spec: Optimize the x and y coordinates of the centers independently in alternating steps (or use a block-coordinate descent approach). While circles are coupled, this can sometimes stabilize the convergence of the SLSQP solver in highly constrained environments.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise Optimization

backlog.spec: Use SLSQP for the initial stages where the constraints are very active (low radius caps), and switch to L-BFGS-B for the final stage (radius cap 1.0). L-BFGS-B handles box constraints efficiently and might refine the sum of radii better when the packing is mostly feasible.
backlog.title: L-BFGS-B Transition

backlog.spec: During the _repair step, if two circles are overlapping, instead of just shrinking them along the line connecting their centers, add a small random 'jitter' to the center positions (within a small epsilon) before/during the shrink to break symmetry and avoid getting stuck in narrow 'flat' regions of the search space.
backlog.title: Jittered Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of just using SLSQP for the stages, implement a few steps of a custom momentum-based gradient descent after each SLSQP stage. Since SLSQP might get stuck in small local optima, the momentum can help 'push' the configuration into a smoother region of the feasible space. The gradient can be computed analytically for the overlap and boundary constraints.
backlog.title: Momentum-based Gradient Descent Restart

backlog.spec: Modify the _repair function so that when a conflict is detected between circle i and circle j, the reduction in radii is weighted by their current sizes (or inversely by their importance). For example, reducing the radius of the smaller circle less than the larger one might preserve more of the total sum. Specifically, use r_i = r_i * (d / (r_i + r_j + epsilon)) where the weight is proportional to the desired relative size.
backlog.title: Radius-Weighted Repair

backlog.spec: Use SLSQP for the initial stages where constraints are active and non-linear, then switch to L-BFGS-B for the final stages (where radii are larger). L-BFGS-B is generally faster and handles box constraints very efficiently. This could be implemented by performing the final 2 stages of the current cap schedule using minimize(method='L-BFGS-B') after transforming the non-linear overlap constraints into a soft penalty.
backlog.title: L-BFGS-B Transition

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP stage, apply a non-linear scaling to the coordinates. Scale the $(x, y)$ space based on the current average radius. For example, if the average radius is small, 'zoom in' on the center of the square to give the optimizer more numerical headroom for the small movements required to resolve minor overlaps.
backlog.title: Non-linear Scaling

backlog.spec: Instead of optimizing all $2n + n$ variables simultaneously, optimize the centers $(x, y)$ while keeping the radii constant (as targets), then optimize the radii while keeping the centers constant. Repeat this cycle for a fixed number of iterations before the next cap stage. This decoupling can simplify the Hessian approximation for the solver.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise Optimization

backlog.spec: Although the script runs on one thread, we can simulate a 'batch' approach by dividing the time limit into smaller chunks. Instead of one long SLSQP sequence, run many short ones (e.g., 5 seconds each) and keep the best result from each chunk. This increases the diversity of the starting points explored within the time limit.
backlog.title: Parallel Independent Restarts

backlog.spec: Modify the objective function to include a heavy penalty for being outside the unit square: $\sum r_i + \lambda \sum \max(0, r_i - 	ext{dist to boundary})^2$. This allows the solver to 'tunnel' through slightly invalid configurations to find better global optima, followed by a strict repair step at the very end.
backlog.title: Soft Penalty Interior Constraints

backlog.spec: Implement a scheme where the time spent on each restart is proportional to the quality of the result. If a restart produces a very high sum of radii, allocate more time (more SLSQP iterations or more stages) to that specific configuration. If a restart is poor, terminate it early to save time for better candidates.
backlog.title: Time-weighted Best

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed INIT_RADIUS, initialize the radii such that their sum is a random fraction of the maximum possible sum (based on area). Also, initialize the radii with a distribution (e.g., power law) so that a few circles are large and many are small, which often leads to denser packings than uniform sizes.
backlog.title: Dynamic INIT_RADIUS

backlog.spec: Scale the gradient of the overlap constraints by the inverse of the distance between circles. This ensures that circles that are only slightly overlapping provide a smaller gradient than circles that are deeply overlapping, preventing the 'oscillatory' behavior where the solver over-corrects for a minor collision and creates a major one elsewhere.
backlog.title: Normalized Gradient

backlog.spec: Instead of pure SLSQP, use a custom gradient descent loop with momentum (e.g., Nesterov or standard) for a fixed number of iterations. The objective is to maximize the sum of radii subject to a soft penalty for overlaps and boundary violations. After the gradient descent phase, use SLSQP for a final 'polishing' step to enforce hard constraints exactly. This helps escape local optima better than pure SLSQP.
backlog.title: Momentum-based Gradient Descent Restart

backlog.spec: Use the L-BFGS-B algorithm to solve the packing. Since L-BFGS-B handles box constraints efficiently (like keeping centers within bounds), treat the circle overlaps as a penalty in the objective function. Use a high penalty weight that is gradually increased (annealed) during the optimization to ensure the final solution is feasible.
backlog.title: L-BFGS-B Transition

backlog.spec: In the optimization step, normalize the gradients by the magnitude of the radii. This ensures that the optimizer treats changes to smaller circles as being as important as changes to larger circles, preventing the solver from ignoring small circles in favor of making larger ones slightly bigger.
backlog.title: Normalized Gradient

backlog.spec: Replace the hard boundary constraints (c + r <= 1) with a smooth penalty function in the objective, such as a logarithmic barrier or a high-power power law. This allows the solver to 'explore' the space slightly outside the boundary and then be pulled back in, often leading to tighter packings near the edges.
backlog.title: Soft Penalty Interior Constraints

backlog.spec: Optimize the x and y coordinates of the centers independently (or in blocks). Because the overlap constraints are coupled, this is a heuristic, but it can prevent the solver from getting stuck in 'diagonal' local optima where moving in one axis is blocked by a circle that would be clear if moved in the other.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise Optimization

backlog.spec: Modify the repair function so that when an overlap is detected between circle i and j, the amount of shrinkage is inversely proportional to their radii. This preserves the size of larger circles (which contribute more to the objective) while allowing smaller circles to 'give way' more easily during the repair step.
backlog.title: Radius-Weighted Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of a constant INIT_RADIUS, initialize radii based on a power-law distribution or a distribution where the expected sum of radii is 80% of the target. This variety in initial sizes can lead to more diverse starting configurations for the SLSQP solver.
backlog.title: Dynamic INIT_RADIUS

backlog.spec: Modify the solve function to run multiple independent optimization attempts in parallel (using a simple pool if allowed, but since we are limited to one thread, simulate this by batching 4-8 quick 'short' runs before doing one 'long' high-iteration run).
backlog.title: Parallel Independent Restarts

backlog.spec: Implement a strategy where the time spent on each restart is proportional to the quality of the result. If a restart yields a sum of radii significantly better than the current best, allow it more time/iterations in the next phase, whereas poor results are cut off quickly.
backlog.title: Time-weighted Best

backlog.spec: Before starting the SLSQP, apply a non-linear transformation to the unit square (e.g., a slight 'bulge' or 'pinch'). Optimize the packing in this distorted space where the objective is weighted by the local transformation Jacobian, then map the result back to the unit square. This can help find asymmetric high-density packings.
backlog.title: Non-linear Scaling

backlog.spec: Modify the loop in solve to implement a basin hopping-like strategy. After the first full SLSQP solve/repair cycle, each subsequent restart should start from the best result found so far but with a random perturbation (e.g., jitter the centers by a small amount) before starting the staged SLSQP process.
backlog.title: Basin Hopping Restart

backlog.spec: In the _repair function, instead of just shrinking radii based on the maximum overlap, implement a mini-simulated annealing step. For 100 iterations, randomly pick an overlapping pair and move their centers slightly apart or shrink their radii, accepting the move if it reduces the total overlap distance or with a small probability (temperature) to escape local minima.
backlog.title: Simulated Annealing Repair

backlog.spec: Modify the solve loop to keep track of the current best packing. If a new packing is found that is better than the incumbent, increase the remaining time budget for the next solve_once call (e.g., by increasing MAX_ITER), while decreasing the time budget for restarts that do not improve the incumbent.
backlog.title: Time-Weighted Best

backlog.spec: After the final staged SLSQP pass in _solve_once, add a final 'polishing' step using the L-BFGS-B method (via scipy.optimize.minimize). This step should use a soft penalty objective: minimize -sum(radii) + lambda * (overlap_penalty + boundary_penalty), where lambda is large enough to enforce constraints but small enough to allow for smooth gradients.
backlog.title: L-BFGS-B Polish

backlog.spec: Modify the staged SLSQP in _solve_once. Instead of using a global cap for all radii in each stage, apply the cap only to the largest radii currently in the packing. This forces the solver to 'grow' the most significant circles first before allowing smaller ones to expand.
backlog.title: Sequential Radius Growth

backlog.spec: Divide the total time limit into 4 equal chunks. In each chunk, run 4 independent solve_once calls in parallel (conceptually, by running them sequentially but ensuring they each use exactly 1/4 of the total time). Keep the best result found across all 4 chunks.
backlog.title: Parallel Independent Restarts

backlog.spec: Modify the objective function in _solve_once to be -sum(radii) / sum(radii). By normalizing the gradient by the current sum of radii, the optimizer will take more aggressive steps when the sum is small and smaller, more precise steps as the sum approaches the optimum.
backlog.title: Normalized Gradient objective

backlog.spec: Replace the hard constraints in the SLSQP call with a soft penalty in the objective function. The objective becomes -sum(radii) + lambda * sum(max(0, r - (c_x - min_x)))^2 + ... for all boundaries and overlaps. Gradually increase lambda over the course of the staged radius caps.
backlog.title: Soft Penalty Interior Constraints

backlog.spec: Modify the _repair function to include a 'jitter' step. After shrinking the radii to resolve an overlap, add a small random displacement to the centers of the overlapping circles in a direction that moves them away from each other's centers. Repeat this jitter and shrink process 10 times.
backlog.title: Center Jitter Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed number of radius-cap stages, dynamically determine the number of stages or the spacing between caps based on the progress of the SLSQP solver. If the solver converges quickly in a stage, increase the cap for the next stage more aggressively. If it struggles, add more intermediate stages to 'guide' the radii toward larger values.
backlog.title: Adaptive Stage Counts

backlog.spec: In the _repair function, if an overlap is detected between two circles, instead of only shrinking their radii, apply a small random jitter (perturbation) to their centers in the direction that moves them further apart before performing the radius shrink. This helps the solver escape 'locked' configurations where circles are squeezed against each other.
backlog.title: Local Jitter Repair

backlog.spec: Modify the _repair function so that when an overlap between circle i and circle j is detected, the reduction in radii is weighted by their current radii (e.g., the smaller circle shrinks more, or the larger circle shrinks more). Currently, it splits the reduction equally; trying weightings like r_i / (r_i + r_j) might preserve the integrity of larger circles better.
backlog.title: Radius-Weighted Shrinkage

backlog.spec: After the final staged SLSQP run in _solve_once, perform a very short (e.g., 20-30 iterations) L-BFGS-B optimization. Use a soft-penalty objective that penalizes overlaps and boundary violations with high weights to 'polish' the final positions and radii, as L-BFGS-B can be very efficient at local refinement once constraints are nearly satisfied.
backlog.title: L-BFGS-B Polish

backlog.spec: Implement a schedule where the duration of the SLSQP optimization in _solve_once is non-uniform. If a specific random initialization yields a sum of radii that is within 5% of the best-found-so-far, allocate 90% of the remaining `time_limit` to that specific solve. Otherwise, use a standard fractional time.
backlog.title: Time-Weighted Best Restarts

backlog.spec: Instead of using only hard constraints in SLSQP, introduce a soft penalty for overlaps in the objective function (e.g., -sum(r) - lambda * sum(max(0, overlap_distance)^2)). Gradually increase the penalty weight lambda over the stages. This can help the solver navigate through 'infeasible' regions of the search space to find better local optima.
backlog.title: Soft-Penalty Transition

backlog.spec: Before starting the staged SLSQP, sort the circles by their initial radii. In each stage, apply the radius caps specifically to the circles that are currently the smallest. This encourages the growth of smaller circles to fill gaps while keeping the large circles (which are harder to move) relatively stable.
backlog.title: Pre-Sorted Radius Growth

backlog.spec: Modify the _repair step to include a 'push-away' mechanism from the boundaries. If a circle is very close to the boundary (distance < SHRINK), apply a tiny force or jitter to move its center away from the edge, preventing the repair step from 'crushing' circles into the corners of the unit square.
backlog.title: Boundary-Aware Jitter

backlog.spec: Modify the solve process to add circles one by one. For each new circle, run a few iterations of SLSQP to find its optimal position and radius given the existing circles. After adding all 32, run a final collective optimization pass. This 'greedy' constructive approach can be more robust than optimizing all 32 simultaneously.
backlog.title: Sequential Circle Addition (Staged)

backlog.spec: Modify the SLSQP objective function to use a normalized gradient. Divide the gradient of the sum of radii by the current sum of radii at each step. This helps maintain consistent step sizes in the SLSQP solver as the radii grow larger, potentially preventing the solver from becoming 'stiff' or unstable in the later stages.
backlog.title: Normalized Gradient Scaling

incumbent.description: Gradual radius scaling: run SLSQP in stages with a cap on every radius (0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.5, then 1.0), warm-starting each stage from the previous one, to avoid early local optima.

memo:
Helped: only the schedule change in slot 2 (staged radius caps 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, ...). It scored -2.9364, which is -0.0112 against the previous incumbent. That is well above the noise sd of about 0.0034, and it is close to the published ~2.9370. It is still a single, unreplicated run.

Did not help: repair tweaks (slots 0, 1, 6), init changes (Sobol slot 3, Beta slot 10, greedy slot 9), the penalty objective (slot 4, +0.0105), capping only some radii (slot 8, +0.0114), the sum(r^1.5) objective (slot 34, +0.0001), and the randomized iteration cap and ftol (slot 23, +0.0010). Slots 5, 14 and 17 were within noise.

Slots 11 (-2.9396) and 12 (-2.9379) beat the incumbent, but each is a single run and the gaps (-0.0031, -0.0014) are under the noise sd.

Next: replicate the incumbent once. Then replicate slots 11 and 12 (basin hopping, annealing). Then tune the stage count, cap values and iterations per stage. Avoid more repair, init or penalty ideas. Many proposals were aborted as duplicates, so check the table first.
